summary: Pivoted Document Length Normalization is a distinct post-processing technique that operates on cosine-normalized scores after initial TF-IDF computation. It differs from peer candidates: Maximum TF Normalization works at the TF stage (pre-scoring), IDF Lookup is a term-weighting component, and Vector Space Similarity is a retrieval-stage operation. The candidate addresses a specific problem (length bias in cosine-normalized ranking) with an empirically-grounded method (pivot point selection). No redundancy detected with peers, and support evidence confirms this is an established technique from authoritative IR literature.
